acceptance: A DuckDB TPC-DI run at scale 3 or 5 produces a PASSED result with TPC_DI_RPS, full audit evidence and the owner's label.
Only DuckDB can run TPC-DI, and only the generate, load and power phases.

description:
## Problem
Every TPC-DI entry point still refuses. With the metric, the evidence block and the validator rules in place, DuckDB can be reopened.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- Label, exactly: "Derived from TPC-DI. Not an audited TPC result; not comparable to TPC Benchmark Results." (CLI, bundle, site)
- Bundle: "a `benchmark.tpcdi` block holding the generator identity and row counts, per-batch elapsed times, the metric (`th`, `ti1`, `ti2`, `tpc_di_rps`), the audit outcome (status, tests total and OK, failed test names, SQL hash, substitutions), visibility executions, the validity flag and the label. Timed rows are named `TDI_HISTORICAL`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_1`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_2`. Result schema takes the next minor version."
- "No compliance class for TPC-DI, plus a rule that TPC-DI never counts as 'official' in the results database."
- "A single-platform TPC-DI cohort may be published as a documented shallow cohort ... The seed workflow regains TPC-DI cells only for platforms that pass the audit."
- Status becomes `experimental`. "No TPC-DI run is published until a DuckDB run passes the full audit."
- 2026-11-21, other phases: "TPC-DI supports only the generate, load and power phases."
- 2026-11-21: generation refuses a scale below 3 ("TPC-DI data generation needs a whole-number scale factor of 3 or more. Got: {sf}."), so a below-floor result can only arrive as a bundle from elsewhere; the validator and admission still refuse it with the reason text.

## Change
Registry: status `experimental`, default scale 5, list 3, 5, 10, 100, and the owner's description: "TPC-DI data integration benchmark: historical load, two incremental updates and the automated audit, on DIGen data." The run gate opens for DuckDB only. Only the generate, load and power phases are accepted for `tpcdi`; any other phase (throughput, maintenance, statistics, warmup) is refused with the owner's message; iterations above 1 are refused with the owner's message. The builder may now mark a result PASSED under the rules of the previous step. The label is printed and stored. Changelog fragment.

## Decision gates
The registry description is the owner's text, verbatim. No result is published by this pull request.

## Verification rubric
Pass: `--iterations 2` refused with the exact message; `--phases throughput` and `--phases warmup` refused with the exact message; through `make heavy-run`, `benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpcdi --scale 3 --phases generate,load,power` and the same at scale 5 produce PASSED results with tpc_di_rps and the label verbatim; `scripts/validate_submission.py --require-manifest` accepts the staged bundle; the three negative controls from the milestone still fail the run; another platform is refused; `make pr-preflight` passes; the soundness review of the head is a success.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message, label text or name (option, configuration key, result field, file name, test hook) the owner has not already chosen is chosen by the implementer following existing BenchBox conventions and the specification, and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). Texts the owner has chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) are used verbatim.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. Delivery follows the batch plan on tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120: a batch member ends at a landing report and its batch has one final pull request; a serial item has its own pull request.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in `_sources/tpc-di/`, `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/` and `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/tools/`. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- Owner, 2026-11-21: "The specification wins without asking. Every difference, and any behaviour of the project that is kept, goes in a catalogue I approve at the milestone stop. A difference from the DuckDB implementation not in the catalogue is a finding that blocks the step." The catalogue is `DEPARTURES.yaml`; every entry of the comparison's expected-differences list must cite a catalogue row. After the milestone stop, a new catalogue row in which BenchBox follows the specification is listed in the pull request; a row that would keep behaviour of the Databricks project that departs from the specification stops for the owner's approval (owner, 2026-11-21).
- The agent never contacts bankmark, the TPC or the Databricks project's author.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
